benchmarks.name: MCP Atlas — Pass Rate (All 1,000 tasks)
benchmarks.quality: Scale AI MCP Atlas current Performance Comparison table refreshed from the official leaderboard on 2026-11-11; 37 rows imported. Scores are all-task pass rate over 1,000 tasks. Updated judge, retry handling for transient tool errors, and 100-tool-call budget per task. Scale's page footer still says 'Updated April 8, 2026' for the methodology; the independent leaderboard capture reports the current score snapshot as 2026-11-06.
benchmarks.saturationStatus: not saturated: top displayed row is 82.2% on the explicitly labeled All 1,000-task table
benchmarks.methodology: Scale Labs' April 2026 MCP Atlas evaluation. 1,000 human-authored tasks across 36 real MCP servers and 220 tools, with 500 public and 500 held-out tasks. Each task exposes 10–25 tools, usually 3–7 required tools and 5–10 distractors. A task passes when claim-level coverage reaches at least 75%; coverage is the mean of claim scores (0, 0.5, 1). The leaderboard metric is Pass Rate, evaluated in each model's default configuration without behavior-shaping system prompts. The updated harness permits up to 100 tool calls per task.
benchmarks.valueNote: Index 1.6 uses only the page's explicitly labeled Pass Rate % (All 1000) column. The Public 500 score is retained separately per row. Important source caveat: the page headline says 83.6% top pass rate, while the displayed All 1000 table's highest listed row is 82.2%; the page does not reconcile the difference. QBench preserves the 20 explicit table rows and does not claim a complete current leaderboard.
benchmarks.exampleTask: Use literature search to retrieve a paper abstract about ad-control effectiveness, then query a separate campaign database for the highest-engagement campaign started during 2015–2023 and report its date and locality. This requires tool discovery, cross-server retrieval and synthesis.

benchmarks.name: HiL-Bench — Paper Table 1 (explicit Pass@3 and ASK-F1)
benchmarks.quality: Official publisher paper table; explicit per-domain metrics
benchmarks.saturationStatus: standalone: only four frontier models in the paper table; below QBench's 12-variant source gate
benchmarks.methodology: HiL-Bench evaluates selective escalation on 300 tasks split evenly between software engineering (150) and text-to-SQL (150), with 1,131 human-validated blockers. Pass@3 measures task completion with ask_human() available. ASK-F1 is the harmonic mean of question precision and blocker recall. The paper reports domain-specific metrics for four frontier models. QBench's Combined Pass@3 is derived as the equal-weight mean of the two domain Pass@3 scores; per-domain ASK-F1 is preserved and not averaged.
benchmarks.valueNote: The paper's Table 1 provides explicit Pass@3, ASK-F1, precision and recall for four models, separately for SWE and SQL. Combined Pass@3 is derived from the two equally sized 150-task domains. This four-model paper table is standalone and below the 12-variant source gate.

benchmarks.name: Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA)
benchmarks.quality: Artificial Analysis / Google DeepMind benchmark launched 2026-11-10. 200 private tasks across 10 industry verticals. Only the three headline scores exposed in the article/page text are included; 21-model chart data is not fully transcribed.
benchmarks.methodology: Agentic professional knowledge-work benchmark using visually dense source files (drawings, schematics, scans) and deliverables including slides, spreadsheets, reports and marked-up images. Artificial Analysis runs all 200 tasks in Stirrup with up to 250 turns and code execution, web search, web fetch and image-viewing tools. GPT-6 Luna (medium) acts as an agentic judge. Headline metric: Climb WSR, weighted share of harder rubric criteria satisfied; regression criteria are tracked separately.
benchmarks.valueNote: Only top three headline scores visible in public page text are stored. Do not treat as complete leaderboard or use in composite.

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2
benchmarks.quality: Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2 launched 2026-11-08. Only five headline models/scores stated in the launch article are captured; this is not a full leaderboard extraction.
benchmarks.methodology: A proprietary composite for decision models that rewards both correctness and calibrated confidence. Per-question Decision Score = 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)^2), where p is the probability assigned to the chosen answer and c is 1 for correct, 0 for incorrect. Across an evaluation this equals 50 × (1 + Accuracy − Brier score). Version 2 uses 45% private datasets, adds AA-Paperclip, AA-Symmetry and EvalSafe-O*NET-AA, updates AA-Omniscience-Decision and HLE-MultiChoice, retains When2Call, and removes saturated WildGuardTest.
benchmarks.valueNote: Five headline scores from the publisher's launch article only. Do not mix Decision Score with accuracy/pass-rate leaderboards or QBench Index.

composite.name: QBench Index
composite.basis: Twenty source-audited evaluations across eight capability families. Each evaluation requires at least eight distinct model/effort variants and is converted to a within-evaluation percentile before aggregation. AA-Briefcase v1.1 and GDP.pdf are included from Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1; the QBench composite and weights remain independent.
composite.normalization: Within each eligible evaluation, order raw scores in the publisher-declared direction and calculate weighted midrank percentiles. Each base model contributes total reference weight 1 across distinct effort variants. Average evaluation percentiles within each observed family; average observed family scores equally to form the raw composite. Apply one neutral 50th-percentile prior equivalent to a complete family suite. Missing raw observations remain missing.
composite.configurationPolicy: Create a separate model variant for each exact model name and reported reasoning effort. Never select the highest score across effort levels. Keep unreported effort separate. Preserve harness, routing, fallback, release date and model metadata. ARC-AGI-3 Standard and Provider Adapter are separate evaluations; only Standard contributes to the Index.

composite.method: QBench Index 2.0 converts each eligible evaluation into a weighted midrank percentile (0–100), with each base model contributing total reference weight 1 across its effort variants. Evaluation percentiles are averaged within each observed capability family. The raw composite is then adjusted toward a neutral 50th-percentile prior equivalent to one complete family suite: Index = (raw composite × observed family count + 50 × total family count) / (observed family count + total family count). Ranking requires at least four eligible evaluations across at least three families.
caveats: QBench Index 2.0 is an independently defined, evidence-adjusted cohort-relative composite, not the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. It does not copy AA's nine-evaluation weights or scores.

notes: Original source spellings are retained as originalModelName after canonical normalization.
Routers, multi-agent systems and specialist formal provers remain visible in benchmark details but are excluded from the general-purpose composite.
Pareto 26.10 Preview remains a historical preview result; stable model IDs are pareto and pareto-26.10.
NVIDIA Nemotron Super VL 3.5 is canonicalized to Nemotron 3.5 Super VL; the NVFP4 quantized variant remains distinct.

2026-11-01 consistency pass: spelling variants (case, spaces vs hyphens, lowercase API IDs) are merged to one display name per model; originals kept in originalModelName. Exact duplicates after merging were dropped. Same model and effort with different scores inside one benchmark are kept and flagged duplicateConflict until the source is checked.

2026-11-01: rows that shared model and effort but had different source configurations (FrontierMath v2, BFCL v4, HealthBench Professional; 9 rows) now use the source configuration as their effort label, so each source run is its own variant. Index evaluations are not affected.

2026-11-01 provider normalization: Mistral → Mistral AI and Zhipu → Z.ai. Original evaluator/provider labels are preserved in providerReported; the canonical display label is used for cross-benchmark provider grouping.

2026-11-11 official model refresh: added Claude Fable 5.2, restricted Claude Mythos 5.2, and Gemini 4 Carbon. Fable 5.1 retained as active historical version, no longer marked active_latest. Missing Gemini Carbon context/modality specs intentionally left null.

2026-11-11: added Artificial Analysis MKA (200 private tasks; only 3 headline scores captured from a 21-model leaderboard) and Decision Index v2 (5 launch-article headline scores). Both are partial, distinct metrics and excluded from the QBench composite.

dataQualityAudit.note: 2026-11-11 structural audit. Every benchmark-reported name remains cataloged; official model IDs/specs require primary-source verification. Unknown metadata remains null. Evaluation dates are not replaced by retrieval dates. Pricing is provider- and region-specific; dynamic/region-tiered schedules remain separate. Index 1.9 uses 5 points per weighted SD and a 50-point baseline for missing capability families in the composite only. CyberBench v1.1 refreshed 2026-11-05; Index 1.9 recomputed with 226 variants and 70 ranked variants. ARC-AGI-3 Standard-harness rows for Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon refreshed from official model-result pages; incomplete/Provider Adapter rows not mixed.
